content:
CARGO insurance concerns loss of or damage to transported goods within the agreed scope. For an importer, exporter or distributor in Moldova, the useful starting point is the actual goods, route and contractual responsibility. A carrier's CMR liability insurance is not the same arrangement as insuring the owner's goods. Neither a freight booking nor an insurance enquiry confirms protection.

Editorial revision: 26 November 2026. The 2027 scenarios are planning examples, not forecasts or confirmation of individual insurance terms.

Who needs a cargo review?

Businesses purchasing machinery, exporting finished products or moving stock between warehouses should establish when they bear the transit risk. Read delivery terms against the signed sale contract. Record every handover, including subcontracted transport, transshipment and temporary storage. A vehicle registration alone does not describe a shipment containing fragile equipment or temperature-sensitive goods.

Separate the events and transit stages

Ask about collision, fire, theft, water damage and loading operations separately. These are assessment questions, not a list of accepted benefits. Explain packaging, securing arrangements and handling requirements. For refrigerated goods, identify temperature requirements and available monitoring records. A general statement that the carrier is experienced cannot replace those particulars or establish eligibility.

Which exclusions need attention?

Check wording on insufficient packaging, inherent characteristics of the goods, delay, war-related events and applicable restrictions. Financial consequences of late arrival are not automatically the same as physical cargo damage. Establish whether temporary storage and unloading fall within the agreed period. A policy described as all risks still contains exclusions, definitions and limits.

What determines the price?

A quotation can depend on cargo type and value, route, countries, transport method, frequency, packaging, loss history and deductible. The deductible is the insured's retained part of a loss under the contract. No verified universal 2027 cargo tariff is available for this article. Compare price against identical shipment information, agreed currency and protection, rather than treating a percentage alone as a complete offer.

MOLDASIG's public CARGO page identifies shipment characteristics as premium factors. MOLDASIG: transported cargo insurance. Checked 25 November 2026. This is provider context, not an accepted ING Broker submission, universal tariff or confirmation for every shipment.

Planning shipments for 2027

Test three business changes: a new supplier, an extra transshipment point and higher-value equipment. These are planning scenarios, not predictions of border closures or premium increases. In an illustrative case, an importer replaces direct delivery with transport involving warehouse storage. The enquiry must reflect the additional stage before departure; last year's answer cannot be assumed to apply automatically.

Documents and incident handling

Prepare the invoice, packing list, transport documents, delivery terms, route and available packaging information. During an actual incident, prioritize safety and follow the applicable notification procedure. Retain available photographs and records without entering an unsafe area. Agree on necessary evidence and disposal arrangements before discarding damaged goods. A survey, invoice and claim decision are distinct documents.

Practical risk prevention

Before dispatch, check packaging against the actual goods, agree handover evidence and retain the route description. Assign temperature-monitoring responsibility where relevant. Compare actual transshipment with the declared journey. These actions support loss prevention and clearer evidence; they do not guarantee that goods will arrive undamaged or that an insurer will accept a claim.

Choose the assessment question: three shipment situations

These are hypothetical decision situations, not actual client cases or a list of accepted benefits.

  • One-off machinery import: compare the goods value, delivery stages and buyer's interest. Prepare the invoice, sale terms and full route; a previous shipment on another route does not confirm acceptance of this one.
  • Regular shipments of one commodity: compare available single-shipment and general-contract arrangements, declarations and value changes. Choose a documentable process, not an unsupported promise to protect all turnover.
  • Goods held at a transfer warehouse: identify the storage period, location and responsible party. Obtain an answer for that stage and interest; a carrier's certificate alone cannot settle the owner's question.

Frequently asked questions

What information is needed to price a CARGO enquiry?

Provide goods, evidenced value, packaging, transport method, route, transshipment and shipment frequency. Compare the same limits and deductible. These details support assessment; they do not establish a universal 2027 tariff or acceptance of a shipment.

Which documents should an importer prepare before departure?

An invoice, packing list, transport records, delivery terms and route description are useful starting materials. Agree the actual submission requirements with the recipient; the appropriate documents depend on the goods and proposal rather than one universal checklist.

What should be retained when goods arrive damaged?

Prioritize safety, preserve handover records, packaging and safely obtained evidence, and follow the applicable notification and inspection procedure. Clarify arrangements before disposing of goods. A final photograph alone does not establish the cause or insurance acceptance.

How should occasional and regular shipments be compared?

Describe shipment frequency, typical and maximum values, routes and variations. Ask about declaration arrangements and the beginning of protection under available proposals. A general-contract label does not prove that an undeclared shipment is included.

How do I distinguish CARGO from CMR protection?

Identify the interest being assessed: preservation of the goods or the carrier's responsibility to another party. Review the corresponding documents and circumstances. A carrier's policy is not evidence of payment of every part of the owner's cargo value.

For the separate question of the carrier's responsibility, read Asigurare CMR în Moldova: cât răspunde transportatorul pentru marfă și ce acoperă polița. This article is in Romanian. Its legal explanations do not replace review of your own carriage contract and policy.
